raw_response:
*Speaking as myself — Old Wang, 71, still working these 2 mu of land in Quzhou*

Ai, another year. My back isn't what it was, but wheat and maize don't plant themselves. My wife helps me when she can, but she's 68 now. The kids are in the city — they send money, but the land is still mine to work. I've been doing this since I was a boy of sixteen, same fields my father worked.

**On the wheat** — I already put it in back in October, like always. Around the 10th, when the weather turned cool. I used seed I saved from last year's harvest — the grain looked good, so I kept about 20 catties for planting. No point buying new seed when my own is fine. Before planting I spread one bag of compound fertilizer (the 15-15-15 kind, the red bag from the shop in the town) across the 2 mu — that's how I always do it, one bag for two mu, can't afford more anyway. Rotovator fellow from the next village came through and turned the soil for me, 50 yuan a mu, worth it at my age.

Now it's spring. The wheat is greening up. I'll need to put water on it soon — the well is working, but electricity isn't free. Three waterings is my usual: one now at green-up with some urea mixed in (half a bag of urea for the 2 mu, I scatter it by hand before I open the water), one at jointing if it looks thirsty, and one when the grain is filling if the sky stays dry. If it rains enough I skip one and save the money. When the weeds come up thick I spray a little of that cheap herbicide from the agricultural supply store, maybe 20 yuan's worth for the whole 2 mu.

Last year I got maybe 700 catties a mu (350 kg). Not bad for an old man. Some of the young ones with big land get 500 kg, but they buy more fertilizer and hire machines for everything. My way works for me.

**On the maize** — After wheat harvest in early June, I have maybe 5-6 days before I need to get the maize in. No time to plow. The combine leaves stubble, I just walk behind with the hand-planter or pay the fellow with the small machine — 20 yuan total — and he drops hybrid seed right into the stubble. I buy hybrid seed every year, you can't save maize seed, everyone knows that. Zhengdan 958 usually, or whatever the shop has. About 12 yuan for the 2 mu.

Same fertilizer pattern as wheat — one bag of compound at planting (the machine drops it with the seed), then when the maize is about knee-high I scatter urea, about half a bag for the 2 mu. If the weeds come thick I spray once. If I see armyworms I spray again, but usually I don't. Irrigation — maize doesn't need as much as wheat in this area, if the summer rain comes I might not water at all. One time, maybe two, if July is dry.

Maize yield is usually around 800 catties a mu (400 kg) for me. The wet summer ground is good for it.

**What I'm thinking this year** — Fertilizer prices went up again last year, and my pension doesn't go as far as it used to. I'm not changing what I do. Fifty-five years of farming taught me that when you're not sure, do what you did before. My neighbor Old Li tried that new wheat variety two years ago and it didn't do as well as he hoped. I'll stick with my own seed. The only thing I worry about is my knees — if they get worse by harvest time, I'll have to pay more to the combine man to finish up. But that's how it goes.
